label_key.measured: Read on the cited page during this research run.
label_key.inferred: Not read on a cited page: general knowledge of the city, a search-result summary, or a reading of the evidence. Check before it goes on the public site.

notes: Scope: things that belong to all of Taipei, 1985 to today. Nothing here repeats an item in ximen.json, dadao.json or xinyi.json (ids checked on 2026-11-21).

How pages were read: Chinese Wikipedia pages were fetched as plain text through the Wikipedia API and the quoted facts were found by text search; four pages (垃圾車, 垃圾費隨袋徵收, 統一超商, and the English pages) were read through a fetch tool that returns quotes. A fact is labelled measured only when its sentence was seen.

Photo licences were read from the Wikimedia Commons API (LicenseShortName) on 2026-11-21. The photos themselves were not opened, so every visual detail that is not quoted from a page is labelled inferred and should be checked against the photo before modelling.
The 'location' field says where the real thing is and suggests a spot on the square; every suggested spot is inferred, since the square is an invented plaza.

No-politics rule: 圓山大飯店, 大安森林公園, SARS and the 2017 Universiade each touch something political on their source page. The public text here leaves that out and each item says so in its unknowns, so CJ can drop the item.

No-logo rule: the convenience store, breakfast shop, YouBike dock, MRT sign, public phone and EasyCard reader should carry plain text or invented names only. Two reference photos show a real chain store; they are for layout only.
Three generations of place are mixed here on purpose (1980s bus, 1996 MRT, 2012 bike dock); which year the square is set in is (unknown — needs CJ).

Second run, 2026-11-21 (events): Chinese Wikipedia pages were fetched as plain text through the Wikipedia API; five news pages (CNA twice, SETN, Storm, yam) and the English MSI page were opened through a fetch tool that returns quotes. A fact taken from a web-search summary is labelled inferred.
Event reference photos are Wikimedia Commons category pages whose existence was checked through the Commons API; the files inside were not opened and their licences were not read.

places.zh: 捷運木柵線（文湖線）高架站
places.en: MRT Muzha Line elevated station (today the Wenhu Line)
places.years: Works began late 1988; opened 1996-03-28; 內湖 section added 2009-07-04
places.history_en: Taipei's first metro line, and the first metro to run in Taiwan. The city decided on a medium-capacity system in 1983, partly because the new zoo in 木柵 was expected to draw more than 60,000 visitors a day, and chose the French Matra system in 1987. Cracks found in the viaduct pier caps in 1993 and a fire during train tests delayed the opening. Free trial rides began on 27 February 1996 and paid service started on 28 March 1996, with 42,548 riders on the first day. The 內湖 section opened on 4 July 2009 and the whole route is now the brown 文湖線.

places.zh: 聯營公車站牌與老公車
places.en: City bus stop with an old joint-service bus
places.years: Joint service since 1977; stored-value card 1995-10-25; EasyCard on buses 2002-09-30
places.history_en: Before 1976 each Taipei bus company had its own routes, numbers and paper tickets. A joint-service system (聯營) was set up so one ticket worked on every bus: routes 201 and 202 started on 1 January 1977 and the first 33 joint routes ran from 30 April 1977. Stop signs, once round, square or plum-blossom shaped depending on the company, became one round sign with a pink base. A magnetic stored-value card for buses arrived on 25 October 1995, ran alongside coin fares, and was withdrawn on 8 October 2003 after the EasyCard took over.

places.en: The garbage truck that plays music
places.years: Music boxes brought in 1980s–2000s; recycling trucks from the 1990s; per-bag fee from 2000-07-01
places.history_en: In Taipei there are no street bins for household rubbish: the truck comes to the corner at a set time and neighbours walk out to meet it. It announces itself with one of two piano pieces, 少女的祈禱 (Maiden's Prayer) or 給愛麗絲 (Für Elise), played from a music box brought in from Japan between the 1980s and 2000s. Who chose the tunes is no longer known; one story credits the health official 許子秋. From the 1990s a recycling truck follows behind, often playing 酒矸倘賣無. Since 1 July 2000 the rubbish must be in the city's paid bags.

places.years: First 美而美 opened 1981 on 八德路, Taipei; over 1,100 franchise shops by 1992
places.history_en: The Western-style breakfast shop on every Taipei corner began in 1981, when 林坤炎, who had worked at a plastics company, sold hamburgers from a cart beside a vocational school and then opened a shop called 美而美 on 八德路. It sold sandwiches and hamburgers; others copied the idea and the name, which led to trademark suits from 1988 that ended in 1994. By 1992 his chain had passed 1,100 shops. Today these shops also sell 蛋餅, 蘿蔔糕, milk tea and soy milk, beside the older Chinese-style shops with 燒餅, 油條 and 豆漿.

places.years: First chain store opened 1980-02-09 on 長安東路; 1,000th store 1995; bill payment from 1998
places.history_en: The first chain convenience store in Taiwan opened on 9 February 1980 in a lane off 長安東路 in Taipei; the page calls it the first 24-hour convenience store on the island. The business lost money at first and was folded back into its parent company in November 1982. Then it spread: the 100th store in 1986, the 1,000th in 1995, the 2,000th in 1999. In 1998 the stores began taking telephone bill payments, later adding utilities, parking fees and fines, which is how the corner store became the place where Taipei pays its bills at midnight.

places.years: Trial from 2009 in 信義; second-generation bikes July 2012; YouBike 2.0 from 2020-01-15
places.history_en: Taipei's public bicycles started in 2009 as a small trial in the 信義 district, built and run by a Taiwanese bicycle maker for the city, and at first few people used them. In late July 2012 new stations opened across the city with a second-generation bike, orange frame and yellow mudguards, rented with the same EasyCard used on the metro, and the docks beside MRT exits became part of the commute. A lighter-install version, YouBike 2.0, began a three-month test around 公館 and the 臺大 campus on 15 January 2020 and replaced the old docks.

places.years: 士林市場 built 1913, opened 1915; city monument 1998; stalls moved 2002-10-14; rebuilt market opened December 2011
places.history_en: The night market is where Taipei eats after dark, and 士林 is the largest in the city. It grew around the 士林 public market, built in 1913 and opened in 1915, beside the 慈諴宮 temple, on a spot where farm goods were once traded before going down the river. The market building became a city monument in 1998. On 14 October 2002 the food stalls moved to a temporary market across from MRT 劍潭站 because of ventilation, hygiene and safety problems; the rebuilt market was finished in December 2011 and its basement food court began trial opening on 24 December 2011.

places.years: First station about 1891; third building closed 1986-02-24; present building opened 1989-09-02
places.history_en: The city's front door. The first Taipei station opened around 1891 and the present one is the fourth. The third-generation building closed on 24 February 1986 after its last Lunar New Year rush and was pulled down from 1 March as the railway through the city went underground. The present station opened on 2 September 1989, Taiwan's first underground railway station: six floors above ground and four below, 149 metres long, 110 wide and 48 high, with a large central hall. Its roof earned it the nickname 披薩屋. The metro, the high-speed rail and the airport line later joined it below ground.

places.history_en: The red palace on the hill that people see from the highway on the way into the city. The hotel stands on 劍潭山 above the 基隆河; its lodging began in May 1952 and the main building was completed in 1973. At 87 metres it was the tallest building in Taiwan from 1973 to 1981, and it is one of the tallest buildings in the classical Chinese style anywhere. On the morning of 27 June 1995 a welding spark during roof-tile repairs set the roof on fire, at about 80 metres up, and the building was restored and reopened in 1998.

With no room to grow, it moved to 木柵 and opened there on 31 October 1986 on a site of 182 hectares, now 165, the largest zoo in Taiwan. events.history_en: Taipei Arena, a 15,000-seat hall on the site of the old city baseball stadium, opened on 1 December 2005 and quickly became the stage every singer in Taiwan wanted. On the night of 10 June 2006 the 17th Golden Melody Awards, the biggest prizes in Chinese-language pop, were handed out there, hosted by 陶晶瑩 and 徐熙娣 under the theme "Music Orz". Fans lined the red carpet outside on 南京東路 to see the nominees walk in. The ceremony has returned to the Arena many times since, and a concert there is still a mark that a singer has made it.

events.en: NBA Taipei game: Jeremy Lin comes with the Rockets
events.history_en: On Sunday 13 October 2013 the Houston Rockets played the Indiana Pacers in an NBA preseason game in Taipei, with the Taiwanese-American guard 林書豪 (Jeremy Lin) leading the Rockets a year and a half after "Linsanity". Taiwan had no hall built to NBA standard, so the floor and the scoreboard screen were flown in and assembled, to match a game in the United States exactly. It was the second NBA game in the city after one on 8 October 2009. Tickets were gone quickly, and for a generation of students who stayed up for his games it was the first chance to watch him play at home.

events.history_en: On 6 January 2014 the panda cub 圓仔 was shown to the public for the first time at Taipei Zoo, six months after she was born there on 6 July 2013 as the first giant panda born in Taiwan. events.en: The Pokémon GO crowds at Beitou Park
events.history_en: In August 2016, days after the phone game Pokémon GO opened in Taiwan, word spread that rare monsters appeared at 北投公園 beside 新北投 station. Night after night crowds of players filled the park and ran together across the road whenever a rare one showed up on screen. The Central News Agency reported on 21 August that the rush had brought illegal parking and bins overflowing with rubbish, and that the hot-spring association and other local groups organised volunteers to pick it up, about 100 kilograms in a day. Video of the running crowd was shown around the world.

events.history_en: From 19 to 30 August 2017 Taipei hosted the 29th Summer Universiade, the first time Taiwan held the world university games. The opening and closing ceremonies were at 臺北田徑場. The city turned out: 720,000 tickets were sold, 87 percent of all seats and the highest rate in the games' history. The home team won 26 golds, its best result, and two wins are still talked about. The weightlifter 郭婞淳 took gold at 58 kilograms with a world-record clean and jerk of 142 kilograms, and the javelin thrower 鄭兆村 won with 91.36 metres, the first Asian athlete to throw past 90.

events.history_en: Nuit Blanche is a free all-night arts event that began in Paris in 2002; Taipei held its first in October 2016 in the old west side. The second edition moved to the student quarter of 公館. From 6 p.m. on 7 October 2017 to 6 a.m. the next morning, close to 100 artworks and performances lined a two-kilometre route through 臺灣大學, the bookshop and café lanes of 溫羅汀, and the 客家文化主題公園. The opening parade went down the university's palm avenue and light was projected onto the main library. The event moves to a new part of the city each year.

events.history_en: The Taipei Lantern Festival has been run by the city since 1997 and changes neighbourhood every few years. From 11 to 20 February 2022 it was held in 士林 for the first time, to bring people back to the night market and nearby shops after the pandemic. The main lantern, TAIPEI 40, was a red and white flying saucer seven metres across and four metres high; "40" sounds like 士林, and the designer took the idea from the planetarium and science museum nearby. It was the first main lantern to perform hanging from a crane. Lantern zones ran from the 劍潭 night market to the 芝山 riverside.

events.zh: 周杰倫「嘉年華」：大巨蛋第一場售票演唱會
events.en: Jay Chou's Carnival: the first ticketed concert at Taipei Dome
events.history_en: Taipei Dome was first proposed in 1991, broke ground in 2012, stood half-built for years and finally opened on 2 December 2023 with a baseball championship. A year later, on 5 December 2024, 周杰倫 (Jay Chou) opened four nights of his Carnival tour there, the first singer to hold his own ticketed concert in the 40,000-seat stadium. About 38,000 people came on the first night; doors opened at 5 p.m. and the Central News Agency reported that the crowd moved in without crushing. 張惠妹, 五月天 and many overseas acts followed within months, and Taipei at last had a hall big enough for stadium tours.

events.history_en: Fancy Frontier, known as FF, is one of the two big fan-made comic fairs in Taiwan and is held mainly in Taipei. The first two editions were at the 世貿 second hall; FF3 to FF24 filled the 臺大體育館, FF25 to FF28 moved to the 爭艷館 at 花博公園, and later editions have gone back and forth between the two. FF24 had 1,700 stalls over two days. In August 2023 FF41 ran for three days for the first time. For students it means queuing from dawn in summer or winter break, cosplayers posing outside, and going home with a bag of self-published books.

events_old_history.history_en: On 28 March 1996 the 木柵線 began paid service and Taipei finally had a metro, after eight years of roadworks that people called the dark age of traffic. The line had been ready late: cracks were found in its pier caps in 1993, a train caught fire in testing that May, and a full safety review ran in 1995. Free trial rides from 27 February 1996 let the city try it first. On opening day 42,548 people rode. Ten years later the whole network carried more than a million riders a day, and by 2019 more than two million.

events_old_history.en: The 921 earthquake as felt in Taipei
events_old_history.history_en: At 1:47 in the morning on 21 September 1999 a magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck 集集 in 南投, about two hundred kilometres away, and shook for around 102 seconds. Taipei felt intensity 4 to 5 and the whole island lost power at once when a main substation and a transmission tower failed. In the city one building fell: the twelve-storey 東星大樓 at 八德路 and 虎林街, where 87 people died or were never found. It was rebuilt on the same site and finished in August 2009. Across Taiwan 2,415 people died.

events_old_history.history_en: On 1 July 2000 Taipei began charging for rubbish by the bag. From that day household waste could only go into the truck in official city bags sold at convenience stores and other shops, so the more a family threw away, the more it paid, and anything sorted for recycling went free. The page read for the date says the policy brought a considerable drop in waste; an English page says the compulsory bags cut Taipei's household refuse by two thirds. The blue bag and the evening walk to the truck became a daily habit across the city.

events_old_history.history_en: Typhoon Nari came ashore on the night of 16 September 2001 and stayed over Taiwan for 49 hours and 20 minutes, a record. On 17 September the Taipei weather station measured 425 millimetres of rain in one day, the most in its 105 years. River water poured into the east of the city through an unfinished dike near 南湖大橋, hit 昆陽站 first and ran down the tunnels, flooding the 板南線, the 淡水線 and Taipei Main Station. Repairs took three months and the whole network was running again on 15 December. Flood-line markers remain in sixteen stations.

events_old_history.history_en: In June 2002 Taipei began issuing a contactless stored-value card, first at ten metro stations and then everywhere from 12 June. On 30 September 2002 it went live on all buses in greater Taipei as well as the metro, so one tap covered a whole commute and the paper bus tickets and magnetic cards faded out; the bus stored-value card was withdrawn on 8 October 2003. The company behind it had been set up by the metro operator on 6 March 2000. More than a hundred and ten million cards have been issued since.

events_old_history.history_en: Taiwan's first suspected SARS case was reported on 14 March 2003. For a month the cases came from abroad; then infection spread inside the city-run 和平醫院 on 中華路, and on 24 April the hospital was sealed with people inside. The first death in Taiwan came on 27 April, and 仁濟醫院 was sealed on 29 April. In May the government requisitioned masks, and passengers on flights had to wear them. On 5 July 2003 the WHO removed Taiwan from its list of affected areas, the last place in the world to come off it.

events_old_history.history_en: On 4 July 2007 Taipei opened its first sightseeing cable car, 4.03 kilometres from the zoo up to the tea hills of 貓空, with four passenger stations and a French-built system. The first weeks were rough: it stopped several times on opening day, and on 21 July a failed drive wheel left 322 riders hanging in their cabins for two hours. After a typhoon in September 2008 washed away ground beside a tower, the line shut from 1 October and returned in March 2010. Glass-floored cabins called 貓纜之眼 were added on 2 November 2010.
